summary: Round r1 (restricted network). Three methodologically distinct sources were located and are kept separate: (1) NRB BoP remittance series (FY basis, workers' and personal remittances) for the remittances/GDP ratio with NSO nominal GDP; (2) NLSS IV 2022/23 statistical report and microdata for household receipt shares by province and remittances by source (survey, includes informal channels); (3) KNOMAD/World Bank bilateral remittance matrix (modelled corridors, calendar year). NRB is not confirmed to publish remittances by sending country; a secondary source attributes a Gulf share to NRB and must be traced to an original NRB document before use. All values pending. A published critique of NLSS IV data quality is flagged for investigation.

findings.claim: Q1: Personal remittances and workers' remittances, FY2024/25 and FY2025/26 (NPR and USD), and ratio to nominal GDP on the same Nepal FY basis.
findings.note: Required: NRB CME annual tables (23C-L01, 23C-L02); NSO nominal GDP for the same FY (from 16A/NSO national accounts).

findings.claim: Q1: Remittance inflows by source corridor - survey basis (NLSS IV, India / other countries and by country from microdata).
findings.note: Required: NLSS IV remittance chapter tables and weighted microdata tabulation (23C-L03, 23C-L04).

findings.claim: Q1: Remittance inflows by source corridor - modelled basis (KNOMAD bilateral matrix, Nepal as recipient).
findings.note: Required: latest BRE vintage (23C-L05, 23C-L06) with methodology note (23C-L07).

findings.claim: Q1: Any NRB-published estimate of remittances by source region (Gulf, Malaysia, India, other).
findings.note: Required: original NRB document; secondary mention located only (23C-L13 and news); do not use until traced.

findings.claim: Q2: Share of households receiving remittances, by province (seven provinces) and urban/rural.
findings.note: Required: NLSS IV remittance chapter tables by province (23C-L03) or microdata tabulation (23C-L04), with standard errors.

findings.claim: Q2: Remittance share of household income / consumption by province and quintile.
findings.note: Required: NLSS IV income-source tables or microdata.

findings.claim: Remittances/GDP uses the NRB numerator and NSO nominal GDP for the same Nepal fiscal year; calendar-year WDI ratios are cross-checks only and are not mixed with FY data.

NLSS (survey, includes informal channels and domestic transfers), KNOMAD (modelled) and any NRB source-region split (formal channels) are three different concepts and are reported side by side; conflicts are documented via find_conflicts, never averaged.

data_gaps: NRB remittances by sending country: not confirmed as published; required document is an NRB table or survey of remittance by source country with period.
Informal (hundi) remittance volume: no official estimate located.
NLSS IV data-quality concerns (23C-L15) require comparison with NLSS III and Census 2021 before use.
Province-level remittance receipts after 2022/23 (no annual survey).
KNOMAD latest vintage and whether updates continued after KNOMAD's wind-down need confirmation on retrieval.

assumptions.text: Personal remittances (BPM6) is the headline concept for remittances/GDP; workers' remittances is reported alongside.
Household receipt share uses NLSS IV definitions (any member receiving remittances in the reference year).

challenges.text: Accept 16B challenge: EXP-01 corridor shares will be three separate values (NLSS survey, KNOMAD modelled, NRB formal-channel if located). The EXP-01 value field should hold remittances/GDP only.
Consumption and poverty parameters sensitive to remittances must use NLSS IV provincial receipt shares with standard errors once retrieved; national averages hide provincial dependence.

Potential conflict: NLSS IV remittance incidence vs earlier NLSS and Census-based migration incidence; public critique of NLSS IV data exists. Escalate if values diverge beyond tolerance after retrieval.

uncertainty: High. No values retrieved. Corridor shares are conceptually uncertain because official formal-channel data by source country may not exist; survey and modelled values measure different things. Household receipt shares depend on NLSS IV, whose data quality has been publicly questioned.
